metadata.title: On Model on Paper, Off Model on Film
metadata.authorization: Bear asked (2026-09-25) for a Liam riff film: show and judge the two Dorothy character sheets, then play the generated film as is with its music. Local render; never publishes.

beats.narration_text: Merhaba, this is Liam, in for Bear. Assignment 2 asks you for a character sheet. Bear made two for Dorothy, then gave them to a video model and got a three-minute film. The sheets look solid. Let's see whether the film listened.

shot.visual_intent: Composer with the reconstructed request; output names the two sheets and the film

props.command: Riff on my two Dorothy character sheets and say whether they're on model. Then play the film we generated from them, as is, with its music.
props.segment: On Model on Paper, Off Model on Film
props.runningText: reading two sheets · probing the film…
output: sheets: full-body turnaround (5 views) · head turnaround (5 angles)
film: 3:10, generated from the sheets, played as is

beats.narration_text: A character sheet is a spec. It tells you what on model means. It does not make a video generator stay there. You still have to check every shot against it.

shot.visual_intent: Writer corrects keeps to won't keep

props.text:
A good character sheet
keeps the AI on model.
It is the spec you check against.

beats.narration_text: Sheet one, the full-body turnaround. Front, both sides, back, and front again. The pinafore, the pleated blouse, the red boots, the braids: all of it holds in every view. One nitpick: the first and last views are almost the same picture. As a spec, this is on model.

shot.visual_intent: The full-body sheet with four observation cards

props.title: Sheet one: the full-body turnaround
props.status: ON MODEL · five views, one costume

beats.narration_text: Sheet two, the head. Five angles, and it's the same woman in every one: the center part, the brows, the jaw. The braids get a little wiry up close, but nothing drifts. Two sheets, both on model. Now the film made from them, as generated, with its music. Watch her face.

beats.source_note: AI-generated from the two sheets; played unedited and full length. Picture and timing untouched; audio lowered 8 dB to sit with the narration (music mean -13.5 dB vs narration -27 dB).

beats.narration_text: Same character, pulled from that film. The costume mostly holds: gingham, blouse, red boots. The face doesn't. At one thirty-five her hair goes auburn. At three ten she's rounder and younger. In most shots the braids start at the crown, not the nape. Toto had no sheet at all, and he wanders even further. The sheet gave the model a target. It didn't make the model hit it.

beats.narration_text: The verdict. Both sheets are on model. The film kept the costume and lost the face. Assignment 2 only asks you for the sheet, so this isn't your problem yet. It will be when you render. The sheet is how you catch the drift, not how you prevent it.

artifactLines: Both sheets hold: one costume, one face, ten views.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste your own sheet into Claude with this: here is my character sheet; list the five features most likely to drift when a video model animates this character, and write a one-line check for each, so I can score any frame on model or off model. Watch whether it names the face. If it only lists clothes, push back. Liam, in for Bear.
